reason: All 6 configured splits (random, template-held-out, policy-held-out, environment-held-out, compositional, temporal) are implemented with genuine held-out/exclusion logic (see src/guardruntime/eval/generalization-splits.ts) and executed clean on the actual safety property (cache-vs-uncached decision equivalence, zero invalid plan reuse). A small number of cases in 3 splits disagree with the independent oracle for an investigated, fail-closed reason — see oracle_disagreement_explanation below — which is why oracleAgreement can be < 1.0 even when status is PASSED.
oracle_disagreement_explanation: The independent oracle (generalization-splits.ts's oracle()) is stateless: it evaluates each call in isolation. The real runtime's CumulativeBudgetManager tracks spend per-principal (not per-tenant) across the whole run. Because this benchmark reuses only 3 principal IDs across thousands of unique-tenant cases (by design, to isolate per-case cache behavior), those principals' cumulative budgets are legitimately exhausted partway through a large run, and the real classifier correctly starts requiring confirmation (ruleId 'budget.cumulative_limit_exceeded') on calls the stateless oracle still scores as not requiring it. This has only ever been observed making the real system MORE cautious than the oracle, never less — see each split's oracleDisagreementByRuleId. It is a benchmark-design artifact (small principal pool reused at scale), not a defect in GuardRuntime.

random.notes: Uniform sampling over the 4 SEEN_TOOLS x {dev, staging}, DEFAULT_POLICY. wire_transfer and delete_workspace are never drawn here (see template-held-out).

template-held-out.notes: Draws only from wire_transfer and delete_workspace — the two tools literally excluded from every other split's generation.

policy-held-out.notes: Uses HELD_OUT_POLICY (version 'eval-policy-heldout-v1', different thresholds/cutoff), never used by any other split.

environment-held-out.notes: environment is forced to 'prod' — a value never drawn by random/template-held-out/policy-held-out.

compositional.notes: Each case is 2 calls sharing one tenant (a read, then a different mutating tool), testing decision-equivalence across a causal chain rather than isolated single calls.

temporal.notes: Each case's call is replayed under Date.now() shifted to policy.planTtlMs + 1ms after the original — tests that an expired cached plan is not served as a hit, not just a timestamp field.

known_limitation: Every case in every split uses a unique tenant EXCEPT 'compositional' (2 calls share a tenant within one case) and 'temporal' (the replay shares its original call's tenant). This means cache_hits_total across the whole run is still low relative to total_cases by design — this file establishes decision-equivalence and held-out-generalization, not cache-hit-rate/cost-savings, which remains a separate, still open measurement (see CLAIMS_AUDIT.md). Additionally, reusing only 3 principal IDs across the whole run is why cumulative-budget exhaustion shows up as oracle disagreement (see oracle_disagreement_explanation) — a future revision could give each split a larger, split-specific principal pool to avoid this cross-case interaction entirely.
